newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Ershad's love, policy rifts split Bangladesh party.
newsitem.headline: Ershad's love, policy rifts split Bangladesh party.

text.p: Bangladesh's third-biggest political group, the Jatiya Party, was on the verge of a split on Friday over a love affair of party chief Hossain Mohammad Ershad and his policy differences with other leaders.
The lines were drawn after three key party leaders served Ershad a notice at about midnight on Thursday to "quit the party and transfer the party's leadership" to them.

Ershad had "turned the party into his own property and indulged in activities that not only tarnished his personal image but disturbed the party's rank and file", the leaders said in a statement they sent to newspapers late on Thursday.
The rebels, including former prime ministers Mizanur Rahman Chowdhury and Kazi Zafar Ahmed and former deputy premier Shah Moazzem Hossain, said they had conveyed their views to Ershad.
Ershad could not be reached for comment on Friday.

They said the former military ruler released from jail three months ago, "must vacate his position as chairman of the Jatiya Party". His replacement will be chosen in a party caucus the rebels plan to hold in May.
They also charged that Ershad's personal line of thinking had prevented the party, which has 33 seats in the country's 330-member parliament, to play an effective role.
"Rather it (Jatiya) has become a tool in the hands of the ruling Awami League," one Jatiya leader said.
Jatiya extended its support to Awami League of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to form a government after general elections last June.
Hasina appointed Jatiya's secretary-general Anwar Hossain Manju as her communications minister, a move she said was an effort to create a government of consensus.
The opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), headed by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, described Manju's induction as a "pay-back" for Jatiya's support.
The rebel Jatiya legislators also demanded that Manju resign from his ministerial job if he wished to stay in the party. Manju told reporters that he was trying to "patch up things".
Ershad has often said he did not believe in "opposition for opposition's sake", and that he would support the government for good work and oppose it for bad.

The rift in the Jatiya party surfaced in March when Ershad expelled Kazi Zafar Ahmed from the party for criticising the government's policies towards India at a rally in Dhaka. Zafar persuaded Ershad to take him back and even restore his senior position in the party's policy planning council.

Things appeared to unravel again this week when Ershad said in a newspaper interview that he had proposed to marry his lover, Zinat Hossain, a fellow Jatiya leader and legislator, after a 14-year relationship.
Earlier he triggered a family dispute by celebrating his birthday with Zinat, wife of former industry secretary Mosharraf Hossain, instead of his wife, Begum Roushan.
Roushan left Ershad briefly to live with her sister.
Under tremendous pressure from the party and his relatives, Ershad moved to pacify his followers on Wednesday night, saying that "politics (not Zinat) is my first love".
He also promised not to do anything that would harm the party's interests.
In a surprise move on Thursday, the 68-year-old former army lieutenant-general said he had severed his relations with Zinat and asked her to refrain from all Jatiya Party activities.
Ershad, who seized power in a bloodless coup in 1982, was deposed in an opposition-led people's uprising in 1990, and was sent to jail. He was freed in January.
